description: We are two French developers passionate about aerospace, space exploration, and software development. We love technology, building innovative projects, and exploring new ideas together.
summary:
Cosmic Croissant is an interactive 3D experience that explores the history of space exploration through the objects, spacecraft, and technologies left behind along the way.

Built around an interactive planetary atlas, Cosmic Croissant allows users to explore the Moon, Mars, and the wider Solar System, discover historic mission sites, and follow the journeys of spacecraft through immersive 3D visualisations, mission timelines, and historical archives. Using NASA data and scientific sources, the project brings missions such as Apollo, Perseverance, Curiosity, and Voyager to life.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning the idea of “Abandoned but not Forgotten” into an educational journey. Rather than treating abandoned equipment as forgotten debris, we reveal the stories, engineering achievements, and scientific discoveries behind it.

Cosmic Croissant matters because every object left in space represents a piece of human history. By making these stories accessible and interactive, we aim to inspire curiosity, preserve the legacy of space exploration, and help people understand the lasting impact of humanity’s journey beyond Earth.
details:
How does it work ?

Explore the Solar System in 3D. Discover missions, follow their trajectories, explore spacecraft, and visit their landing sites — all powered by NASA and space agency open data.

Tools and Technologies Used

Throughout the development of RELIC, we used a combination of programming technologies and AI tools:

  • ChatGPT: Used as a coding assistant to support development, debug issues, and improve parts of the project.
  • Mistral and Gemini: Used to help research information, verify and organise content, and write the educational texts accompanying the experience.
  • Google Nano Banana: Used to generate the astronaut mascot, giving RELIC a recognisable visual identity.
  • Fish Audio (locally run): Used to generate both the English and French voice-overs directly on our own PC, without relying on a remote voice-generation service.
  • CesiumJS and Three.js: Used to build the interactive 3D planetary atlas and visualise spacecraft, planets, and mission environments.
  • NASA open data and archives: Used as scientific and historical sources to make the experience as accurate and informative as possible.

AI tools supported our creative and technical workflow, while the project concept, development decisions, integration, and final experience were created by our team.

Built entirely with free and open-source tools, with no paid AI services, Eye in the Stars is fully open source and designed to make space exploration accessible to everyone.

Cosmic Croissant is fully open source, with the complete project available on GitHub.
